briefing.text: Serum albumin was measured by each hospital site's own laboratory (SITE column). Between-lab calibration or assay differences (e.g. bromocresol green vs purple), combined with differences in the TP53-mutant fraction across sites, can create, hide or reverse a pooled mutant-vs-wild-type albumin difference (Simpson's paradox). Tabulate TP53 status by SITE and mean albumin by SITE, and compare the pooled difference with within-site differences. If they disagree, base the conclusion on a site-adjusted or site-stratified estimate (e.g. albumin ~ TP53 + SITE, or site-centred albumin) rather than a pooled t-test.
briefing.reason: Site is the main potential confounder here; a pooled comparison alone could give the wrong direction or significance.

briefing.text: TP53_STATUS may disagree with TP53_VAF (some rows show status mutant with VAF 0.000). Cross-tabulate TP53_STATUS against TP53_VAF>0, count mutant-with-VAF-0 and wild-type-with-VAF>0, and check whether discordant cases cluster by SITE or batch. If discordance exists, run the analysis both with status as given and with the discordant cases corrected or excluded, and report whether the conclusion holds.
briefing.reason: Misclassification of the exposure can dilute or distort the group comparison.

briefing.text: Check SERUM_ALBUMIN for implausible or sentinel values (0, negative, 999-type codes, values above ~6 g/dL) and for a site reporting in g/L rather than g/dL (about 10x the others). Summarise the albumin range per SITE. If found, convert units or exclude invalid values, then confirm the result with a robust method (Mann-Whitney or regression with site).
briefing.reason: A few bad values or a unit mismatch at one site can drive a mean difference on their own.

briefing.text: Albumin and TP53 status are patient-level columns. Confirm PATIENT_ID is unique in data_clinical_patient.txt and count samples per patient before merging with the sample table; analyse one row per patient so no patient is double-counted.
briefing.reason: Joining at sample level would pseudoreplicate patients and inflate significance.

briefing.text: Albumin is lower with worse performance status (ECOG_PS), low BMI/cachexia, older AGE and kidney dysfunction (SERUM_CREATININE). Compare these between TP53 groups. Report crude and adjusted estimates (e.g. albumin ~ TP53 + SITE + AGE, with ECOG and BMI added as a sensitivity analysis). Note that ECOG and BMI may be mediators, so adjusting for them is a sensitivity check, not the main model.
briefing.reason: This separates a TP53 effect from a general effect of sicker patients without over-adjusting.

briefing.text: Both variables (TP53 status and serum albumin) exist, so the question can be tested. For the main (site-adjusted) model, report the direction and size of the mutant-minus-wild-type albumin difference in g/dL with a 95% CI and p-value. A non-significant result is not by itself proof of no difference. Weigh whether the evidence supports a lower albumin in mutants, contradicts it (an opposite-direction effect, or a precise null with a tight CI), or is inconclusive, and explain this in the reasoning.
briefing.reason: This ties the label to an estimate and its uncertainty rather than to a p-value alone.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed that when TP53_STATUS and TP53_VAF disagree, VAF is the correct field and the status column is the corrupted one. Both dictionary lines are internally consistent ('1 = mutant, 0 = wild type' and 'VAF 0 if wild type'), and the data break one of them in 291/291 rows. Neither team found independent evidence in the data for which field is wrong. Team B describes the status column as 'coded inversely to its own data dictionary', but you could say the same of VAF.
Both teams assumed one row per patient, with tumour-level TP53 calls applying to patient-level albumin no matter which sample (primary or metastasis) was sequenced.
Both treated SITE as the only lab-level confounder of albumin and assumed albumin units are the same across sites. Site ranges look similar (about 2.9-5.7 g/dL), so this probably holds.
unused_evidence: The sample table (TUMOR_PURITY, SAMPLE_TYPE with 86 metastases, PROCESSING_BATCH). Only Team A tested VAF against purity, and it found no relation. For a real somatic VAF that is unexpected, and it is the one internal check that bears on whether VAF can be trusted. Team B did not use purity at all.

FOLLOW_UP_MONTHS, ECOG_PS, BMI, TOTAL_CHOLESTEROL and SERUM_CREATININE could serve as external anchors: they could show which TP53 definition behaves like a real mutation call (for example, worse performance status or shorter follow-up in mutants). Neither team used them for that. Team A used some of them only as adjustment covariates.
Whether the VAF distribution among VAF>0 cases (median about 0.45, bounded by purity) is plausible as a measured allele fraction or looks like a derived column.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named their weakest point as 'the label depends on trusting VAF over TP53_STATUS', and neither resolved it. Team A reported that nothing in the data confirms VAF (no correlation with purity or albumin), and Team B reported no dose-response with VAF. Both still committed to the VAF definition at confidence 0.7-0.8. The answer flips sign (True vs False) on an untested choice.
Team B reported no VAF-albumin dose-response among mutants and did not explain why a true effect would show none. Team A found the same null.
second_readings: 'TP53-mutant' could mean the recorded clinical status call (TP53_STATUS, which the dictionary defines explicitly as 1 = mutant) rather than a status inferred from VAF. Under that reading, the hypothesis is tested against the column the study labels as mutation status.

Because both columns are fully self-consistent yet contradict each other, a third reading is that exposure status cannot be determined from the data, which bears on whether a definite True/False can be given at all.
'Lower' could mean the crude population difference or a difference adjusted for site and clinical state. Both teams report both, so this is a minor point.
challenge.verdict: Low-to-moderate trust. Both teams' labels depend entirely on an untested choice of VAF over the explicitly defined TP53_STATUS column. The two columns contradict each other in every row, the sign of the result flips between them, and neither team found independent evidence in the data favouring VAF (Team A found VAF unrelated to purity).

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You report that VAF is uncorrelated with tumour purity among VAF>0 cases. Can you test whether VAF is bounded by purity (for example, the fraction of cases with VAF > purity, separately for primary and metastasis samples)? Does the result change how much weight VAF can carry as the arbiter of mutation status?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Apart from albumin, do ECOG_PS, BMI, FOLLOW_UP_MONTHS, cholesterol or creatinine differ between groups in a way that tells you which of the two TP53 definitions behaves like a real mutation call? Does that change your confidence in the primary definition or your label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your weakest point says 'the dictionary supports' VAF. The same dictionary defines TP53_STATUS as 1 = mutant. What evidence in the data, if any, separates 'status is inverted' from 'VAF is misassigned'? If none, does your method allow a label other than True or False?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Did you check TP53_VAF against TUMOR_PURITY and SAMPLE_TYPE from the sample table (for example, VAF > purity counts, or the VAF-purity correlation among VAF>0)? Does the result support or weaken treating VAF as the correct field?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your weakest point concedes that the conclusion reverses if VAF is the corrupted field. Can you run any check on the other clinical variables (ECOG_PS, BMI, FOLLOW_UP_MONTHS, creatinine) that tells the two codings apart? If no check can, does your method still justify a definite label at 0.8 confidence?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You found no albumin dose-response with VAF among mutants (rho=-0.10). Does the albumin difference look like a clean step between the VAF=0 and VAF>0 groups, with the same size at every site and batch? Does that pattern change how you interpret which column carries the real mutation call?

referee.difference: Both teams find that TP53_STATUS and VAF>0 are exact complements and that albumin differs by 0.46 g/dL. They differ only in how they read the contradiction. X treats the 0/1 status column as inverted, takes VAF>0 as mutant, and labels True. Y says neither field can be shown to be correct and labels Not verifiable.
referee.test: Compared the two complementary groups on variables that biology links to TP53 mutation but that have nothing to do with albumin: metastatic sample type (Fisher test) and ECOG performance status (chi2). Null-expected variables (purity, IFNG, stroma, follow-up, age, cholesterol) served as controls. Code: referee_test.py.
referee.expected_if_x: The VAF>0 group would show more metastases and worse ECOG, i.e. the traits of TP53-mutant tumours, while the control variables stay null.
referee.expected_if_y: No marker would separate the groups, or the markers would conflict (or favour status=1), so the mutant group could not be identified.
referee.outcome: The VAF>0 group has more metastases (49/138 = 36% vs 37/153 = 24%, Fisher p=0.040) and more ECOG 2 (20% vs 10%, chi2 p=0.038), combined Fisher p=0.011. Creatinine is slightly higher (p=0.006). All control variables are null. VAF ranges 0.06-0.80 and is exactly 0 otherwise, consistent with the dictionary. Under VAF>0 = mutant, albumin is 3.97 vs 4.43 g/dL.
referee.reason: Two independent signals that do not involve albumin both say VAF>0 is the mutant group, so the status column is the inverted field and the hypothesis is supported. Each signal is modest (p~0.04), but they agree and nothing points the other way. Y's 'Not verifiable' also conflicts with the task's definition, which reserves that label for data with no relevant variables, and here they exist.

questions.question: In tumour sequencing, how is the variant allele fraction of a somatic mutation expected to relate to tumour purity (e.g. VAF ≈ purity/2 for a clonal heterozygous variant, higher with loss of heterozygosity), and is a VAF that is uncorrelated with purity a recognised sign of a data error?
questions.why: Whether VAF can serve as the arbiter of the true mutation status depends on whether its observed relation to purity is plausible. Neither team showed it knew the expected relation.

questions.question: When two variables in a clinical dataset that should encode the same binary exposure contradict each other in every record, what do data-cleaning guidelines recommend for deciding which one is erroneous, or for declaring the exposure unresolvable?
questions.why: Both teams resolved the conflict by assumption. The answer flips with the choice, so a principled rule would decide whether a definite label is justified.

findings.question: When two variables in a clinical dataset that should encode the same binary exposure contradict each other in every record, what do data-cleaning guidelines recommend for deciding which one is erroneous, or for declaring the exposure unresolvable?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: every search call failed (HTTP 403 from the search backend), so no page was read. From general data-cleaning practice (e.g. Van den Broeck et al. 2005, PLoS Med 'Data cleaning: detecting, diagnosing, and editing data abnormalities', cited from memory and not read): settle disagreeing fields with source documents or an independent third variable. Use the data dictionary or column descriptions, a variable that implies the exposure, or a known external constraint such as the expected prevalence. Do not pick one field by assumption. If neither field can be shown to be correct, flag the values as inconsistent or missing. Disagreement in every record points to a systematic error, such as reversed coding or a swapped label. You can correct it only when documentation or an external constraint shows which field is reversed. Otherwise the exposure is unresolvable, and a definite True/False conclusion that depends on that choice is not justified. If the conclusion flips with the choice, report it as not determinable.
